body:
# Independent audit of the general surface parity roof construction

Audited source:

`candidate 9764a982661d3ddc`.


separately proved background and selection dependencies listed there.
The source proves a boundary-transport repair for a finite compatible
family of full-dimensional continuous fibers. It does not assert OC,
intrinsic boundary geometry for degenerate fibers, or halfspace order
from convex order.

I read the full source, the mixed finite-base density-selection theorem,
the measurable unbounded-density extension in
`candidate 93c94ac2c5c85584`, and the measurable
assembly lemma. I also independently checked the local ball and
dimension-alignment steps of the general conditional surface theorem.
The face-to-normal background bridge is separately proved in
`candidate f38040720425d155`.

## 1. Reference measure and normal exceptional sets

The enlarged normal reference is

    sigma = sum_z S_Kz + sum_(z,w) S_Mzw,
    M_zw=(K_z+K_w)/2.

It is finite, and the normal marginal of the entire original surface
measure is the first sum. Thus every endpoint normal marginal dominated
by that original measure has Radon--Nikodym density at most one relative
to sigma. The same holds for the old tuple's normal marginal because it
equals either endpoint normal marginal. This correctly bounds the
conditional masses needed for compact measurable assembly; bounding only
each labeled body separately would not have been sufficient.

The general ball theorem's triple reference lambda is dominated by
sigma. Where both endpoint conditional measures relative to sigma are
nonzero, t=d lambda/d sigma is positive. Replacing every triple
conditional by t times itself preserves the ball power mean and all
derived density bounds because they are homogeneous of degree one.
Where t=0 there is no positive endpoint flow to treat. Finitely many
labeled triples permit one common sigma-full Borel normal set.

The normals of pair-average bodies are included even where they do not
contact the actual target fiber. They are actual convex-body references,
not arbitrary auxiliary row labels.

## 2. Common tangent dimension is available before roof enforcement

At a fixed good normal u, the triple (K_z,K_w,M_zw) is tight by the
definition of Minkowski averaging. The already proved ball theorem
therefore forces the two positive endpoint faces and the pair-average
face to have one common affine dimension and direction space.

Because every ordered pair is included, comparison across all positive
original conditionals yields one dimension m and one direction V.
This does not depend on an old base-pair assignment, a midpoint already
being on the actual target boundary, or an integer midpoint. It is
therefore valid for the unrestricted product-coupling optimization.

All faces lie in their u-supporting hyperplanes, so V is contained in
u-perp. Consequently normal height is constant on each auxiliary output
level. The orthogonal splitting X=b+y with b in V-perp and y in V
preserves the m-dimensional Euclidean normalization. Real auxiliary
bases (z,b_z) are permitted by the mixed selection theorem, with no
claim that this splitting is a mixed-integer lattice automorphism.

## 3. Temporary capacities are legitimate finite measures

For each source face, the chosen endpoint density is finite and
positive on a marginal-full differentiation set, and is set to zero
elsewhere. Absolute continuity ensures that this modification leaves
the reference measure, and all selected endpoint submeasures, unchanged.

The pair-average target upper-density representative may be infinite
at exceptional points. Nevertheless its integral in the common
m-dimensional affine face is the finite conditional surface mass.
Its exceptional infinity set is H^m-null. The variable-density
selection theorem explicitly permits such target representatives,
first establishes output absolute continuity, and then removes those
null exceptions. Thus no boundedness or upper semicontinuity assumption
has been inserted.

At every finite auxiliary level, summing the finitely many pair-average
upper densities gives a fixed finite capacity measure dominating the
required harmonic expression for every marginal-good endpoint tuple.
The sum is needed only temporarily off the true support graph. The
notation sigma_aux in the source means counting measure on the finite
auxiliary output levels times Euclidean H^m along V.

On a level whose normal height equals the actual target support height,
every producing base pair is tight: the normal height depends only on
its two affine offsets and equals the average support height. Applying
the target version of the ball theorem gives a positive conditional
target face of dimension m and direction V. The pair-average face lies
inside that target face. Equal dimension therefore gives the same
affine hull and the same V-perp offset. Hence there is only one
on-support auxiliary level above a physical output base p.

Replacing all temporary pair-average capacities on that level by the
ONE actual target conditional density is justified pointwise by the
target ball theorem for every producing pair. This is exactly the step
that prevents an extra factor from the number of ordered base pairs.

## 4. The support roof is a valid global finite convex test

For the finite base family, compatibility implies that every convex
combination of lifted support heights with barycenter p in P has
height at most h_Kp(u). The lifted point (p,h_Kp(u)) itself is included.
Therefore the upper boundary of the finite lifted convex hull agrees
with h_Kp(u) at every sampled p, including projection-boundary bases.

Adding the downward vertical ray produces a polyhedron in aff(P)
times R. Its vertical facets describe only the projected domain;
the finitely many nonvertical upper facets yield affine majorants
ell_j. Their minimum equals the support roof on conv(P), and their
affine extensions give a finite concave function on the whole base
space. The rank-zero case is simply a constant roof on a singleton
affine hull, extended affinely.

Thus

    Phi(z,X)=u dot X - min_j ell_j(z)

is an ordinary globally finite convex function. It is nonpositive on
the canonical convex body. It vanishes at all old midpoint outputs.
The selected output belongs to that same body, and its base remains
integer because every product endpoint pair is in one parity class.
Convex order gives integral Phi >=0, while support gives integral Phi
<=0. Hence Phi vanishes almost everywhere on the new output.

This is one valid convex-test application. It does not assume that
individual old base-pair masses survive, that convex order directly
preserves halfspaces, or that a nonsmooth boundary roof is continuous.
The finite polyhedral roof is continuous globally by construction.

Combining its zero set with the unique on-support offset from Section 3
turns the temporary mixed capacity into exactly the actual target
surface conditional measure, once per physical base.

## 5. Parity, measurability, and marked reconstruction

An old integer midpoint has equal endpoint parity. Disintegration over
normal and parity therefore gives equal endpoint submasses. Every
product tuple in one such class has integer midpoint. Lattice
completeness puts that midpoint base in P; compatibility places its
continuous midpoint in the actual target fiber.

The construction gives one target capacity per parity class. Summing
classes costs at most 2^n, exactly as stated. A realized tuple at p must
also have tight support heights, so the stated smaller attainable-class
count is valid. There is no asserted cancellation of overlapping
classes.

Measurable assembly only selects final couplings in fixed physical
coordinates. Their marginal, convex-test, and domination constraints
are countable continuous constraints with Borel kernel right sides.
The separately proved compact selector applies. It never needs a
measurable choice of V, an orthonormal basis, the finite roof facets,
or the temporary density representatives used for pointwise existence.

For source marks, the compact martingale from old to new midpoint laws
preserves the old conditional mean. Retaining the original joint law
of mark, normal, parity, and old midpoint, then drawing the selected
endpoint tuple conditional on its new midpoint, preserves the claimed
joint mark distribution and midpoint mean by the tower property.
The source appropriately does not claim preservation of old marked
endpoint kernels or separate endpoint conditional means.

## 6. Zero face dimension, d=1, and sharpness

If m=0, all relevant faces are singleton points. A strongly convex
surplus optimizer determines the endpoints from the output, so any
output atom is bounded by each reconstructed endpoint atom. The ball
inequality bounds their minimum by the target or pair-average atom.
The discrete fixed-capacity separation argument therefore applies,
without evaluating an m-dimensional harmonic formula at m=0.

For d=1, each interval has two boundary points with unit H^0 mass.
At either of the two normals, all labeled bodies have equal conditional
atom mass after normalization by the common reference. The discrete
selection and finite roof argument apply directly. No surface measure
of negative dimension is used for d=0.

The sharpness family uses identical K at bases [0,2]^n intersect Z^n.
Minus endpoints have bases {0,1}^n; plus endpoints have {1,2}^n. In each
coordinate, an integer midpoint is possible only for endpoint pairs
(0,2) or (1,1), both with midpoint 1. Thus every admissible repaired
output has base (1,...,1). Its mass is 2^n times one copy of the
boundary measure, so a universal coefficient smaller than 2^n is
impossible. The complementary-base, identical-boundary-point coupling
attains equality. This also covers n=0 and the separate d=1 case.

## 7. Scope retained after the audit

The result is a sharp normal-preserving surface parity repair under
the stated finite compatible full-dimensional-fiber hypotheses. It
supplies neither a deterministic OC center nor a numerical cap-payment
inequality. Literal endpoint-midpoint implications for closed ambient
halfspaces remain true for the selected coupling, but arbitrary
first-variation boundary allocations need independent justification.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
